case.summary: Customer C08299 disputes a $30.02 online charge (3581141, 2016-12-28). Every structural attribute of the charge matches the cardholder's own baseline: online product S (87%/85% of history), amount well below mean, a device already seen five times on this card, a region the card has used before, and a model score of just 0.28. Critically, the exact $30.02 amount has been billed three times previously on this card, so the dispute most likely reflects an unrecognised recurring merchant descriptor rather than fraud. The apparent device-ring linkage rests on the generic 'unknown | unknown | unknown | unknown' placeholder and collapses on inspection; none of the genuinely rare device profiles touch this card, and the region 203 newcomer fraud rate (0.14 vs 0.10) is noise. Under R7 and R1 this is a verify-and-warn case, not a block: open a case, contact the customer with the prior identical charges, and leave the card active. Exposure is $30.02, well under the $500/$1,000 thresholds, so no report and no escalation.

evidence_requests.assumed_response: Customer, shown the three earlier $30.02 charges (3342487, 3381749, 3545489), recognises the recurring merchant/subscription and confirms the 2016-12-28 charge is theirs; they had simply not recognised the billing descriptor.
